PD import (user approved 2026-10-24): one stream per target rank, all streams concurrent; each import owns a 64 MiB source buffer cut into 1 MiB chunk slots dealt round-robin to its streams; a chunk holds its slot from source read until its target write completes (RDMA source-buffer semantics), so a stream keeps at most its slot count in flight while adjacent chunks' reads, links and writes overlap on the native timelines.
External producer streams prompt-1 KV tokens; native one-token final-prompt generates the first visible output and pays its complete cost.

Continuous batching: freed slots refill at the next step from the pre-imported requests of their own EP group (4 group(s), up to 2 per group, 8 in total; pool sized from the slots a group frees per step and the steps one import spans at Table I write rates, x4 margin; its KV counts against capacity); final-prompt queries join mixed decode cohorts.

Attention data parallelism over 4 EP groups: each group owns B/ep requests and runs their attention, dense MLP, router and shared expert on its own TP ranks (dense weights replicated per group, KV only on the owner group); MoE experts are shared by native all_to_all dispatch and combine across groups, and every layer ends at one cross-group barrier.

Native layer runs on independent copies of the first continuous-refill boundary are physical; the stationary step, PD-import extra, refill schedule, cohorts and visible Tokens are separate conditional predictions.

Unsampled layers take their class's sampled step: the DRAM row openings that differ between same-class layers because their buffer addresses straddle row boundaries differently are assumed negligible and are not bounded; representative-point full native runs check every unsampled layer against its class interval.
